$about: The parts of ELECTRONICS-DATASHEET.html that are not one row per component: the bus, the control table, the power tree, the pin map, the software map. Rendered by tools/gen_electronics_datasheet.py. The per-component roster lives in electronics/components.json and the vendor facts live in ce-parts/<slug>/; nothing is duplicated across the three.

revision.supersedes: Revision A, hand-maintained HTML with no generator. B is generated; every number traces to components.json, ce-parts/<slug>/, or a named file:line.

architecture_cards.title: Compute
architecture_cards.body: Radxa ZERO 3W — Rockchip RK3566 quad Cortex-A55, Wi-Fi 6 / BT 5.4, 65.000 x 30.000 mm. Runs Armbian; the RK3566's 0.8-TOPS NPU runs a duck detector at 2 Hz, thermal-limited. The store says 1 GB RAM + 32 GB storage and Radxa's own SKU table has no such row — narrowed to two options in ce-parts/radxa-zero-3w.

architecture_cards.title: Actuation
architecture_cards.body: 15 x ROBOTIS DYNAMIXEL XL330-M288-T on one 1 Mbps Protocol-2 TTL bus at /dev/ttyS2 (RK3566 UART2_M0). IDs 10-14 / 20-24 / 30-34; mouth = ID 34, excluded from the 14-DoF policy. 270.0 g of the robot's 780 g.

architecture_cards.title: Sensing
architecture_cards.body: Control IMU LSM6DSV16X on the imu_to_dxl board at bus ID 200; an 8x8 ToF that is a VL53L5CX or a VL53L8CX decided at runtime; IMX219 camera behind an M12 lens, mounted inverted; a BMI088 fitted and dormant on the HAT; one mono analog microphone; two NFC antennas whose reader nothing names.

architecture_cards.title: Power
architecture_cards.body: An NP-F550-form-factor 2S Li-ion pack, removable, in a bay measured 38.7310 x 21.1721 x 70.9231 mm. No fuel gauge and no ADC: state of charge is the voltage the servos report. USB-C brings 5 V in; the FUSB302 PD node is disabled and the fitted CC die is an ET7301B.

servo_bus.lede: One wire does everything. Fifteen servos and the IMU bridge share a single 3.3 V-logic (5 V-tolerant) TTL half-duplex UART at 1 Mbit/s under DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0. There is no second bus and no second port (robotd-design.md).
notes: Physical layer is NOT RS-485: 3-wire TTL half-duplex with no direction GPIO in the firmware, so a self-steering transceiver on the HAT switches direction in hardware (community reading of the source).
Chain order, measured off the placements by the wiring lane: HAT -> 34 -> 33 -> 32 -> 31 -> 30 -> IMU 200 -> both legs; longest hop 165 mm through the +/-170 deg head-yaw joint.

WHERE THE CHAIN FORKS IS AN ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. wiring/cables.json puts the branch at the imu_to_dxl board, which needs three connectors. A Dynamixel bus is multidrop and forks equally well at a Y-splice — Open Duck Mini v2's own wiring diagram shows a two-port controller and a T. See ce-parts/microduck-imu-to-dxl connector_count.

boot.title: Written once at boot (robotd, per servo)
boot.code:
return_delay_time = 0    (vendor default 250 -> 0)
baud_rate        = 3    (1 Mbps)
pwm_slope        = 255
shutdown         = 52   (overload | overheat | electrical shock;
                        vendor default 53, INPUT VOLTAGE ERROR bit cleared)
boot.note: Rationale (model.rs): the default 250 is 500 us turnaround x 16 devices = 8 ms/tick, 40 % of a 20 ms budget — so it is zeroed. The shutdown byte is the one to read twice: clearing Bit 0 switches off the servo's over-voltage protection, and it has to be switched off because the pack reaches the servos at 6.6-8.2 V against a 6.0 V rating. See §7.

tick.title: Read every tick / every second
tick.code:
50 Hz loop (20 ms):
  sync_read  regs 124-136  IMU block + 15 servos
             (present pos / vel / load)
  sync_write goal positions
1 Hz slow:
  read regs 144-146  present_input_voltage (0.1 V/LSB),
                     temperature
Gains: P = 200, I = D = 0
  standing_gain_ratio 0.8 - gain_limp 50 on predicted fall
tick.note: The imu_to_dxl board answers ID 200 in the same sync_read: register block at address 124 carries 6 bytes gyro (int16, 17.5 mdps/LSB) + 6 bytes SFLP game-rotation quaternion (x/y/z as fp16, w reconstructed). One IMU, one code path (imu.rs).

rows: NP-F550-form-factor 2S pack -> banana contact PCB -> HAT
all 15 servos DIRECTLY; the HAT's regulators
State of charge is read back out of servo register 144. At 6.6 V smoothed the robot sits down and powers off.
USB-C (PD disabled, so default 5 V) or a HAT buck from VBAT
'in-robot power comes from the battery via the HAT regardless' (i2c3.dts). The buck's part number is CANNOT DETERMINE.
codec, ToF, BMI088, camera, I2C pull-ups
The HAT's regulator part is CANNOT DETERMINE. The ToF branch cannot be a naive 3.3 V — see §7.
IMX219 VANA 2.8 V + VDIG 1.8 V per its own table.

resolved_note.title: The servo supply — no longer an open question
resolved_note.body: Revision A of this document said: 'Either production servos are stock parts run over-spec, or there is a regulated rail we cannot see. A meter on a servo VDD pin settles it.' Pollen's own source answers it. duck-control/src/model.rs:102-112, verbatim: 'There is no fuel gauge and no ADC. The only measurement available is what the servos report as their own supply (crate::bus::DynamixelIo::bus_voltage), which is the pack seen through the bus.' A regulator between pack and servos would make that reading a constant and useless as the fuel gauge it is. Corroborating it, SERVO_EEPROM writes shutdown = 52 where the vendor default is 53 — the single cleared bit is Input Voltage Error, a fault that a 5 V rail could never trip. THE SERVOS SEE THE PACK. Full verdict, with the stall-current extrapolation: ce-parts/xl330-m288-t component.json voltage_band_verdict.

power_tree.drop_note: Bus voltage drop is nevertheless in spec: 21 AWG at 6.6 V still delivers 6.05 V to the far ankle (wiring/drop.json), 0.550 V of drop from the HAT at 8.2 V.

rows: servo bus via the HAT's transceiver
BCLK / LRCLK / DIN / DOUT, MCLK 12 MHz
pin_map.note: Connectors NOT identified in any published source, and each is a real gap for a shop: the servo-bus JST type and pitch on the HAT, the battery contact geometry, the CSI ribbon length and its module-end connector, the mic and speaker terminals, and the NFC antenna feed.
pin_map.mount_frame_note: The Radxa's own mechanical interface — the 4 x O2.8140 mm mounting pattern on 57.8429 x 22.8662 mm and the 40-pin header body frame — was measured off Radxa's raster drawing on 2026-09-02 and is in ce-parts/radxa-zero-3w/iterations/v0.0.1/cad/interfaces.json. It is what a HAT layout starts from. WHICH CORNER IS PIN 1 IS NOT DIMENSIONED and a board laid out the wrong way round is scrap.

rows: /dev/ttyS2 - rustypot XL330 - 50 Hz ONNX policy (obs[61] -> act[14])
/dev/i2c-pihat (i2c-3) - 8x8 at 15 Hz - generation chosen at runtime by an ID read
rkisp mainpath - H.264 via Rockchip MPP - WebRTC :8443 / :8080
ALSA card 'aic3104' - capture on MIC2R/LINE2R pin 16 - mic wake-word CNN - per-robot voice bank
Bluetooth - same mapping as the sim's gamepad path
software.note: All JSON-RPC over unix sockets. Full software map with file:line: docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md.

custom_boards.name: RPI Robot HAT (P1)
custom_boards.body: On the Radxa's 40-pin header. Carries the TLV320AIC3104 codec (0x18), the dormant BMI088, the ToF via a Stemma J5 connector (0x29), the half-duplex bus transceiver, the battery-to-board power path and a 10 kohm I2C pull-up pair (R12/R13). Disables the Radxa's PD node. IT MUST ALSO CARRY AN AUDIO POWER AMPLIFIER that no source shows: the codec's recommended minimum load is 16 ohm and its maximum output 30 mW into 16 ohm, against an 8 ohm 2 W transducer.

custom_boards.name: imu_to_dxl v2 (P2)
custom_boards.size: unknown — no mesh, no photograph, no drawing
custom_boards.body: Presents an LSM6DSV16X as a Dynamixel Protocol-2 slave at ID 200, register block 124. Rides the servo bus and takes its power from it. MCU, transceiver and firmware are unpublished. Its connector count is CANNOT DETERMINE and — contrary to what this repo previously argued — is not forced by the bus topology.

custom_boards.name: Banana battery-contact PCB (P3)
custom_boards.body: Clamped in the trunk by the printed banana_pcb_locker; carries the pack's contacts to the HAT. Measured clearance to the pack: 0.0145 mm. Shape, contact layout and contact rating unpublished — and it carries the whole servo-bus current, which at 15 servos stalling extrapolates to 36.07 A.

figure_notes.electronics/1-block-diagram.svg: READ ONE BOX WITH CARE: the Radxa block prints '1 GB · 32 GB'. That is Pollen's store listing, and Radxa's own SKU table (RAD-DOC-0084 Rev 1.10 §7 p.8) has no 1 GB + 32 GB eMMC row — 32 GB eMMC pairs only with 4 GB DRAM. The block diagram is generated by electronics/gen_ee.py, which is a different lane's file and was not edited here; the narrowed verdict is in ce-parts/radxa-zero-3w electrical.host.json identity_vs_fitted and in §12 row E8.
figure_notes.electronics/2-schematic-hat.svg: The HAT sheet shows SPK+ / SPK- leaving the board with no amplifier between the codec and the connector. That is what the published sources show and it is not buildable: the codec's recommended minimum load is 16 ohm and its maximum output 30 mW into 16 ohm (SLAS510G p.7, p.11) against an 8 ohm 2 W transducer. §12 row E2.
